answer:
**Under the current policy: 1 day per week.** Remote work is limited to a maximum of 1 day per calendar week, and each remote day requires written approval from your direct manager [remote_work_policy_v2 § 2. Office Attendance]. The same section requires at least 4 days per calendar week in your assigned office [remote_work_policy_v2 § 2. Office Attendance].

**Important: the documents disagree on this number.** Three ingested documents state different limits:

| Document | Limit | Effective date |
|---|---|---|
| remote_work_policy_v2 (ACME Hybrid Work Policy v2.0) | max **1 day/week** | 2025-06-01 |
| remote_work_policy_v1 (Remote Work Policy v1.0) | up to **3 days/week** | 2024-01-01 |
| sample_policy (RW-2025-014) | tiers of **3, 4 or 5 days/week** | 2025-03-01 |

- v1.0 says employees "may work remotely for up to 3 days per calendar week" [remote_work_policy_v1 § 2. Remote Work Allowance].
- The sample policy's tier table lists Bronze 3 days/week, Silver 4 days/week and Gold 5 days/week remote [sample_policy § Policy Number: RW-2025-014. Effective Date: March 1, 2025.].

v2.0 is the latest-dated remote work policy from the same owner (People Operations) and is the natural successor to v1.0, so 1 day/week is the best reading of the current rule — but note that the sample policy (effective March 1, 2025) still describes arrangements of 3–5 remote days per week, which is incompatible with v2.0's 1-day cap. The documents do not state which one prevails where they overlap, so if you are relying on this for an actual arrangement, confirm with People Operations. The scanner also flags a scope conflict between v1.0 (engineering, design and support only) and v2.0 (all full-time employees in every function).

Sources:
- [remote_work_policy_v2 § 2. Office Attendance]
- [remote_work_policy_v1 § 2. Remote Work Allowance]
- [sample_policy § Policy Number: RW-2025-014. Effective Date: March 1, 2025.]
